title: Tatarstan Airlines 363
summary: Tatarstan Airlines Flight 363, a Boeing 737-500, was on final approach to Kazan International Airport when the crew determined the aircraft was not properly configured for landing. The crew initiated a go-around maneuver using TOGA mode, retracted the landing gear, and reduced flaps from 30 to 15 degrees while manual control was engaged. After reaching 700 meters altitude, the aircraft entered a steep nosedive with pitch angles reaching minus 75 degrees. The aircraft crashed in a 75-degree nose-down attitude at 242 knots, killing all 50 occupants.

title: LAM Mozambique Airlines 470
summary: LAM Mozambique Airlines Flight 470, an Embraer 190 with 33 occupants, crashed into Bwabwata National Park in Namibia on 29 November 2013. While cruising at 38,000 feet between Maputo and Luanda, Captain Herminio dos Santos Fernandes deliberately changed the autopilot settings to descend to 592 feet below sea level, locked the co-pilot out of the cockpit, and initiated a rapid descent at approximately 100 feet per second. The aircraft struck terrain with no survivors. Investigation revealed the captain had experienced personal tragedies including his son's death exactly one year prior.

The aircraft descended rapidly at a rate of about 100 feet per second for six minutes until radar contact was lost at 3,000 feet above sea level.

summary: A police helicopter operated by Bond Air Services, carrying three crew and responding to search tasks, crashed into The Clutha pub in Glasgow after both engines flamed out.
